options.content: A group whose members pay regular contributions towards funeral costs
options.rationale: Correct: it supports a bereaved family.

options.content: A group of elders who decide where in the village each person must be buried
options.rationale: It is a savings group, not a group of elders deciding burial sites.

options.content: A meeting of spirit mediums who bring home the spirit of a person after a year
options.rationale: That describes a ceremony, not a society.

options.content: A school club that teaches students the history of the cemeteries in the district
options.rationale: A burial society is a mutual-help group.

explanation: Members of a burial society contribute small amounts so that the society can pay towards funeral costs and support a bereaved family.

options.content: A savings or lending club
options.rationale: Correct: members contribute regularly and take turns to receive the pooled money.

options.content: A rain ceremony held at a sacred place in the Matopo Hills each year
options.rationale: That is a different practice (mukwerera).

options.content: A title given to a chief by the elders at his installation
options.rationale: A mukando is not a title.

options.content: A song sung at a funeral to honour the dead person and comfort the family
options.rationale: A mukando is a savings club, not a song.

explanation: Mukando is a Shona savings or lending club based on trust and regular contributions.

stem: How does a marriage create inter-dependency between families?

options.content: The two families give up their own names and take the name of the chief
options.rationale: Marriage does not change family names in this way.

options.content: The two families can no longer visit one another once the wedding is over
options.rationale: The families remain connected.

options.content: The two families agree to share one house and to have only one head for both
options.rationale: They do not share one household.

options.content: The two families gain new relatives and duties to one another
options.rationale: Correct: marriage joins families, not only individuals.

explanation: A marriage alliance brings obligations of hospitality, support and attendance at ceremonies between the two families.

stem: Which example shows mutual help at a life event?

options.content: A family buys a new radio for its own use and does not tell the neighbours
options.rationale: That is not mutual help.

options.content: A family moves away from the village without telling its relatives where it went
options.rationale: That reduces contact.

options.content: A family refuses to attend a wedding because of a quarrel over land
options.rationale: That shows a threat to inter-dependency.

options.content: Neighbours bring food and firewood to a family that has had a death
options.rationale: Correct: the community supports the bereaved.

explanation: At funerals, weddings and illness, relatives and neighbours give practical help.

stem: Rudo's father is ill. His brothers take turns to stay with him, neighbours bring food and the church sends two women to cook. Which idea is shown?

options.content: The decline of family ties because of migration to the towns
options.rationale: The example shows strong ties.

options.content: Inter-dependency among relatives, neighbours and a religious community
options.rationale: Correct: several groups give help.

options.content: The role of a chief in settling a dispute between two clans
options.rationale: No dispute is mentioned.

options.content: The use of a mukando to raise money for the school fees of the children
options.rationale: No savings club is mentioned.

explanation: Relatives, neighbours and a church together support a sick family member.

stem: Which pair correctly links a religion with a teaching on community support?

options.content: Islam: the church is like a body with many parts (Acts 2:44-45)
options.rationale: These are Christian references.

options.content: Judaism: believers are brothers and sisters (1 Corinthians 12:12-27)
options.rationale: That is a Christian reference.

options.content: Christianity: the church is like a body with many parts (1 Corinthians 12:12-27)
options.rationale: Correct: the parts depend on one another.

options.content: Christianity: believers are brothers and sisters (Qur'an 49:10)
options.rationale: Qur'an 49:10 is a Muslim reference.

explanation: Christians cite 1 Corinthians 12 (the body) and Acts 2 (sharing); Muslims cite Qur'an 49:10 (believers are brothers and sisters).
hints: Check which scripture belongs to each religion.

stem: Which statement is the best-balanced comment on migration and family inter-dependency?

options.content: It ends all links between families because relatives can no longer reach one another
options.rationale: Many families remain connected through visits, money and phones.

options.content: It can weaken daily contact, but money sent home and phones can keep families connected
options.rationale: Correct: it has both effects.

options.content: It has no effect on family inter-dependency because relatives always live near each other
options.rationale: Migration changes where relatives live.

options.content: It always strengthens families because everyone earns more money in a different place
options.rationale: Not every migrant earns more, and distance can weaken ties.

explanation: A balanced answer shows that migration weakens daily contact but can also support families through remittances and communication.

stem: Inter-dependency means that people give and receive help.
explanation: True. Help goes in both directions.

stem: Burial societies are open only to people of one religion.
explanation: False. Many burial societies include people of different religions and areas.

stem: Match each threat to inter-dependency with an example.

right.content: a quarrel over inheritance divides a family
a household has too little food to share with relatives
a person puts private success before duties to relatives
relatives move to town or abroad and see each other rarely

explanation: Each threat weakens the willingness or ability to help one another.

hints: Only one reference is from the Qur'an.

stem: What is the Ndebele word for a work party?
explanation: A work party is **ilima** in Ndebele and **nhimbe** in Shona.

stem: State **three** ways in which families depend on one another.

points.description: Marriage alliances or kinship networks
Mutual help at funerals, weddings or in illness
Burial societies, savings clubs or work parties

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: Through marriage alliances and kinship networks; through mutual help at funerals, weddings and illness; and through burial societies, savings clubs and work parties.

stem: Describe how a burial society or savings club helps its members.

points.description: Members make small regular contributions
The group pays towards funeral costs or gives money to a member in turn
No household carries a large cost alone
It builds trust and cooperation, sometimes across religions

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: Members make small regular contributions. The group then pays towards funeral costs or gives a member the pooled money in turn, so no household carries a large cost alone. It also builds trust and cooperation among members, who may belong to different religions.

explanation: One mark for each accurate point.
hints: Say how it works, and what it achieves.

stem: Explain how religion helps families to depend on one another.

points.description: Shared rituals bring families together
Developed: naming, weddings and funerals in IR, and festivals in other religions, make relatives meet and renew their bonds
Places of worship give a meeting place
Developed: at church, mosque or synagogue members meet regularly and support the sick and the poor
Teachings encourage care for others
Developed: for example, zakat in Islam and the teaching of sharing in the first Christian community encourage believers to help those in need

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: Shared rituals bring families together: naming, weddings and funerals in IR, and festivals in other religions, make relatives meet and renew their bonds. Places of worship give a regular meeting place where members support the sick and the poor. Teachings also encourage care for others; for example, zakat in Islam and the sharing of the first Christian community encourage believers to help those in need.

hints: Use three points: rituals, meeting places, teachings.

stem:
**Source A** — an extract from a fictional magazine article, Bulawayo, 2026 (invented for this question)

> When Mr Dube died, his burial society met the cost of the coffin. His wife's brothers travelled from Gwanda to help. The church choir sang at the graveside, and women from the neighbourhood cooked for the guests for three days. 'We could not have done it alone,' his daughter said.

Study Source A and answer the questions.

parts.label: (a)
parts.stem: Which idea does the daughter's last sentence best express?

options.content: Families should avoid asking for help from any neighbour or relative
options.rationale: The source shows help being given and welcomed.

options.content: Funerals are best held away from the village where the person lived
options.rationale: Not suggested in the source.

options.content: Families depend on others in times of need
options.rationale: Correct: inter-dependency.

options.content: Burial societies are expensive and should be avoided by most families
options.rationale: The source shows the burial society helping.

parts.explanation: The daughter says the family could not have managed alone.

parts.label: (b)
parts.stem: State **three** groups that helped the family in Source A.

points.description: The burial society
The wife's brothers (relatives)
The church choir or the neighbourhood women

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: The burial society; the wife's brothers; the church choir and neighbourhood women.

parts.label: (c)
parts.stem: Explain **two** ways in which the help shown in Source A reflects the role of religion or community in family life.

points.description: The church choir shows a religious community supporting a bereaved family with worship and comfort
The neighbourhood women and relatives show community responsibility for families in need

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: The church choir sang at the graveside, which shows a religious community supporting the bereaved family with worship and comfort. The neighbourhood women cooked for three days and the wife's brothers travelled to help, which shows the community and relatives sharing responsibility.

explanation: The source shows burial society, kin, church and neighbours helping a family.
hints: Link two details of the source to religion and community.

stem: Themba says: "Families in town do not depend on each other as in the village." Nokuthula says: "They still do, but in different ways."

parts.label: (a)
parts.stem: Give **two** ways in which families in rural areas depend on one another.

points.description: Work parties (nhimbe/ilima) help with ploughing and harvesting
Relatives and neighbours help at funerals, weddings and illness

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: Neighbours help one another at work parties for ploughing and harvesting. Relatives and neighbours also help at funerals, weddings and in times of illness.

parts.label: (b)
parts.stem: Explain **two** ways in which families in town show inter-dependency.

points.description: Burial societies, savings clubs or groups of neighbours pool money for funerals and school fees
Churches, mosques and other faith groups visit the sick and support families

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: Town families join burial societies and savings clubs that pool money for funerals and school fees. They also belong to churches, mosques or other faith groups that visit the sick and support families in need.

parts.label: (c)
parts.stem: To what extent has inter-dependency among families been weakened by modern life?

points.description: Weakened: individualism, migration, pressure of work and cost of living, conflicts over inheritance
Kept or changed: remittances, phones, burial societies, faith communities
A supported judgement

levels.descriptor: Developed explanation of several relevant points or arguments, supported by accurate, specific knowledge and examples, considering more than one side and reaching a supported judgement that answers the question.
Some explanation of one or two relevant factors, or several points described with limited explanation; little or no judgement.
Simple, general or narrative statements with limited relevance to the question; little explanation.
One or two relevant but undeveloped points.

answerSpec.modelAnswer: Modern life has weakened some inter-dependency. Migration, long working hours, the cost of living and quarrels over inheritance make it harder to visit relatives and share resources. However, families also use phones, send money home and join burial societies, savings clubs and faith groups that support them. Inter-dependency has therefore changed in form more than it has been lost, though it is under strain in some families.

explanation: A balanced answer shows both strain and adaptation.
hints: Give evidence of weakening and of adaptation before judging.
